project: Package-Owned Workstation Semantics and Truthful Packaged Factory Graphs
description: Implement Stories 6 and 7 of the Factory Graph Visual UX plan by making the Factory graph package the single projection authority for independent workstation runtime type, scheduling behavior, and guarded-control role; removing missing-metadata exhaustion guesses; and cleaning disconnected Work states from canonical first-party packaged Factory definitions with a catalog regression check. Keep graph hosts, generated artifacts, published packages, documentation, and runtime smoke behavior aligned so downstream HITL, operation-node, and graph-grammar work can rely on a truthful workstation taxonomy.

context.customerAsk: Deliver Stories 6 and 7 of docs/internal/development/plans/factory-graph-visual-ux.md: move workstation type, scheduling behavior, and guard-role projection into ui/packages/factory-graph as the single source of truth; eliminate missing-metadata semantic guesses; remove disconnected Work states from first-party packaged Factories; and add a catalog check that prevents those states from returning.
context.problem: The shared workstation presentation overloads workstation_kind, discards authored workstation type, and treats missing kind and worker metadata as evidence of exhaustion. This can mislabel ordinary or lossy replay nodes and obscure guarded logical controls. First-party packaged Factory definitions also contain states with no admission path, workstation route, invocation return, or implemented lifecycle bridge, so graph, replay, CLI, and published consumers present speculative topology as real behavior.
context.solution: Derive one protocol-neutral workstation presentation from canonical authored Factory definitions with independent runtime-type, scheduling-behavior, and guarded-control axes; merge runtime activity by durable workstation identity; render unavailable semantics as an explicit neutral fallback; and make all shared graph hosts consume that projection. Add a catalog-only semantic reachability check over parsed first-party definitions, remove unimplemented disconnected states from authored sources, regenerate catalog and package artifacts, align docs and smoke expectations, and preserve existing reachable runtime outcomes without changing public schemas or scheduling behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Every user-visible Factory workstation communicates authored runtime type and scheduling behavior as separate semantic axes, and supported guarded logical moves expose their control role, target, and limit without requiring selection.
Missing, undefined, legacy, and unknown metadata uses a documented neutral fallback and never produces a fabricated exhaustion, loop-breaker, repeater, or other special role.

Current activity observe/edit, selected-tick replay, the public Factory graph package, and trace views agree on workstation semantics when the authored definition is available; lossy sources show the neutral fallback.

Every declared Work state in every first-party packaged Factory has a machine-checked implemented role, and a synthetic disconnected state causes the catalog check to fail with the Factory slug and exact workType:state diagnostic.

Canonical packaged definitions, generated catalog and published artifacts, reference documentation, smoke expectations, and rendered graphs agree after disconnected states are removed, while existing reachable invocation and routing outcomes remain unchanged.

Typecheck, focused package/component/catalog/runtime tests, generated drift checks, and required CI pass; there are no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared/generated-file churn are reconciled against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Reject disconnected states in the first-party catalog
userStories.description: As a packaged Factory maintainer, I want the catalog check to reject declared Work states with no implemented behavioral role so speculative topology cannot silently ship as operational graph behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The catalog check evaluates canonical parsed first-party Factory definitions and accounts for states used by external admission, workstation inputs or outputs, onContinue, onRejection, onFailure, classification-route outputs, explicit invocation return, or a named implemented lifecycle bridge backed by direct behavioral tests.
A focused test introduces a synthetic disconnected state and proves the check fails with the Factory slug and exact workType:state diagnostic.
Valid initial, routed, classification-output, failure, rejection, continuation, and invocation-return states are accepted without depending on source-text layout.
Lifecycle exceptions are accepted only when tied to named implemented behavior with direct test evidence; comment-only allowlists do not satisfy the rule.
The stricter rule is limited to the first-party packaged catalog and does not become a blanket validation error for customer-authored, JavaScript-controlled, or externally controlled Factories.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.reviewFollowUp: Restored the shared customer validator's strict completion-state rule and kept recurring-controller and composite-parent allowances inside the first-party catalog. Packaged installation now uses a catalog-owned preparation hook that filters only exact builtin-loop/builtin-quorum lifecycle bridge targets; ordinary named-Factory persistence remains strict. The topology validator tests were split so backend-size and package-maintainability gates pass.
userStories.notes: Implemented the package-owned semantic role validator and focused tests for canonical initial, routed, classification, failure, rejection, continuation, explicit-return, JavaScript-scope, and invocation-schedule overlap states. The first-party catalog gate is wired to the real BuildCatalog path, with route-proven canonical exceptions for the recurring controller and composite-parent lifecycle shapes; ordinary nonterminal Work types remain rejected. Added regression coverage proving disconnected declarations are rejected with the Factory slug and exact workType:state identities. Acceptance audit completed with the focused catalog, canonical-validator, automation, generated-catalog drift, and diff checks passing.

userStories.title: Remove unreachable states from shipped packaged Factories
userStories.description: As a Factory user, I want every Work state shown by a first-party graph to represent real shipped behavior so dashboard, replay, CLI, and package consumers present a minimal truthful topology.
acceptanceCriteria: The goal Factory contains goal:init, goal:complete, goal:blocked, and goal:failed, does not contain goal:execute, and preserves the established repeater and loop-breaker accepted, continue, blocked, and failed outcomes.

Every other disconnected candidate identified by the catalog audit is removed unless an existing runtime operation already produces it and direct behavioral tests prove that behavior; missing lifecycle behavior is deferred to a separate product story rather than faked through projection or UI filtering.
The cleanup occurs in canonical authored Factory definitions, so dashboard, editor, replay, CLI inspection, generated catalogs, and published package consumers observe the same state inventory.

Generated catalog manifests, flattened definitions, embedded assets, and publishable package artifacts are regenerated from authored sources and pass drift verification without hand-editing generated output.
Reference documentation, diagrams or examples, and smoke expectations describe only the retained shipped paths, and a graph projection or browser fixture proves work-state:goal:execute is absent.
Existing invocation and runtime smoke coverage for each changed Factory proves its reachable admission, continuation, rejection, failure, and explicit-return outcomes remain unchanged.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Removed goal:execute, loop-controller:stopped, and quorum task:complete from the canonical authored Factories, regenerated flattened JSON/YAML artifacts and manifest hashes, and aligned the lifecycle reference diagram and automation fixture. Added route-proven canonical validation for recurring controller self-loops and composite terminal outcomes, while retaining rejection for ordinary nonterminal Work types; the first-party catalog gate now runs on the real BuildCatalog path and reports Factory slug plus exact workType:state diagnostics. Published catalog regression coverage asserts the shipped state inventories, and the graph projection test proves work-state:goal:execute is absent. Existing @you/goal, @you/loop, and @you/quorum focused functional suites, catalog generation/check, UI graph test, UI typecheck, UI lint, package-structure, and focused vet pass.

userStories.title: Project workstation semantics from canonical Factory definitions
userStories.description: As a graph consumer, I want one package-owned workstation semantic projection so runtime type, scheduling behavior, and guarded-control meaning remain independent and reproducible across graph hosts.
acceptanceCriteria: The Factory graph package exposes a protocol-neutral projection with separate authored runtime type, scheduling behavior, and derived control role; no new projection writes a single overloaded kind value for multiple axes.

Runtime type provides the primary semantic role for inference, agent, script, poller-run, classifier, logical-move, legacy model values, and unknown future values, using the repository's canonical taxonomy rather than a second divergent enum table.
Scheduling behavior independently represents STANDARD, REPEATER, CRON, and POLLER, including supported lowercase legacy inputs, without replacing the primary runtime-type identity.
Only a supported guarded LOGICAL_MOVE, including a VISIT_COUNT guard, becomes a guarded-control or loop-breaker role; ordinary logical moves remain logical routers and classifiers remain classifiers.
Undefined, incomplete, or unknown semantics resolve to an explicit neutral unknown presentation; the missing-kind plus missing-worker exhaustion heuristic and equivalent semantic guesses are removed.
Authored semantics are joined to selected-tick activity by workstation id, using authored name only for legacy definitions without ids; runtime activity overlays do not overwrite authored semantics.

Pure projection tests cover every supported runtime type crossed with each scheduling behavior, guarded and unguarded logical moves, lowercase legacy inputs, missing values, and unknown future strings.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the package-owned Factory workstation projection with independent canonical runtime-type, scheduling-behavior, and guarded-control axes. Canonical AGENT_RUN, INFERENCE_RUN, SCRIPT_RUN, POLLER_RUN, CLASSIFIER_WORKSTATION, LOGICAL_MOVE, and legacy MODEL_WORKSTATION/MODEL_INVOKE values map through the generated client taxonomy; lowercase legacy values normalize, and omitted/invalid/future values remain neutral UNKNOWN on the affected axis. Supported VISIT_COUNT guards alone produce LOOP_BREAKER; ordinary logical moves and classifiers retain their distinct roles. Authored workstation ids join selected-tick activity overlays, with names used only for id-less legacy definitions, and replay nodes consume the disposable projection without reconstructing semantics from runtime metadata. The former missing-kind plus missing-worker exhaustion presentation and overloaded semanticKind output were removed. Verification: `make typecheck`; graph package typecheck; 53 focused graph tests; 88 client tests; graph build; client generated-contract check; package-boundary check; package pack verification (31 files); and `git diff --check` all pass. Story 004 remains for cross-host visible control-card/browser coverage.

userStories.title: Render consistent workstation meaning across graph hosts
userStories.description: As a Factory user, I want current activity, editing, replay, and trace graphs to render the same workstation meaning so I can trust icons, labels, badges, and guarded-control cards wherever I inspect a Factory.
acceptanceCriteria: Every shared workstation node communicates runtime type through an icon plus visible text or an accessible label, and communicates non-standard scheduling behavior through a distinct secondary treatment that does not erase the primary role.

In the authored goal Factory, execute-goal is visibly and accessibly both an agent-run workstation and a repeater, while goal-loop-breaker is a compact guarded logical-control card exposing its VISIT_COUNT target and limit without selection.

Current activity observe/edit and selected-tick replay resolve semantics from the authored Factory definition; public package replay does the same through FactoryGraphSource.factory; a trace source that cannot recover the definition renders the neutral unknown fallback.

Components treat React Flow node data as a disposable projection and do not reconstruct authored type, behavior, or guards from icons, CSS classes, DOM measurements, or runtime-only topology metadata.
Component tests prove projected metadata drives the visible and accessible node semantics and prove missing metadata never renders exhaustion or another fabricated special role.

Direct browser verification at fit-to-view zoom covers a mixed Factory containing classifier, logical move, guarded loop breaker, inference, agent, script, repeater, cron, and poller semantics, with representative long names at desktop and touch-sized viewports.

Existing loading, empty, error, and success behavior of host graph surfaces remains intact; semantic badges and compact control cards preserve keyboard selection, visible focus, accessible naming, responsive legibility, and localization behavior.
No backend scheduling behavior, public enum, OpenAPI shape, alternate renderer, or unrelated graph redesign is introduced.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.reviewFollowUp: Fixed the review-found empty-string workstation-ID join by normalizing blank IDs before the id-versus-name decision. An editor-flow render regression now proves a legacy blank-ID topology retains authored AGENT_RUN and REPEATER labels; missing metadata remains explicitly neutral.
userStories.notes: Implemented the package-owned shared workstation node and wired current activity observe/edit, factory-definition editing, selected-tick replay, public Factory graph replay, and trace dispatch hosts to the same authored semantic projection. Nodes visibly and accessibly expose runtime type, retain non-standard scheduling as a distinct secondary label/treatment, and render guarded logical VISIT_COUNT controls with their role, target, and limit outside selection state; unknown or lossy sources stay neutral and never infer exhaustion. Host joins are id-safe: authored names are used only for id-less legacy definitions, while runtime topology metadata remains a disposable overlay. Added component, projection, replay, trace, localization, and missing-metadata coverage, plus a mixed Storybook fixture with long names and a fit-to-view touch/desktop browser lane covering classifier, logical move, guarded loop breaker, inference, agent, repeater, cron, and poller semantics. Verification: `make typecheck`; `make ui-test` (355 Vitest files/2,970 tests and 191 Bun-native tests); `make ui-lint`; graph package 54 tests, build, package-boundary, and pack verification; Storybook build; filtered `Mixed Workstation Semantics` interaction test; and direct touch/desktop browser verification all pass. No backend scheduling behavior, OpenAPI shape, or public enum was changed.
